texts: doha about people buying fancy idols at the market and thinking God comes with the purchase
Every Diwali my mother-in-law haggles at the market for a bigger, shinier idol of the deity, and the old one just sits unwanted. Doha for her please
idol, market, bought God
In the market the gods are sold by weight and glitter; can the Unseen be carried home in a bag?

Tell, in a couplet, of the man who walks through the market comparing idols by price and polish, choosing the most beautiful carved image to worship, never wondering how a thing made by hands can hold the Maker.
doha: you plant a seed and it grows but a carved idol never does, so why bow to it
My grandfather, a farmer, once said the seed in the soil is closer to God than the idol on our altar because at least the seed does something. Could you put that in a doha?
A doha about the farmer who knows that a seed becomes a plant while the carved idol he bows to every dawn remains exactly as it was, unable to grow, to speak, or to bless a single field.
idol, seed, lifeless god
The seed breaks open and becomes a plant; the idol sits unchanging, and we ask it for life.
I need two lines about the moneylender who garlands an idol and begs it for more profit while a moth circles a glow near him, burning for a real love that the carved image will never give.
moneylender, moth, idol worship
The moneylender in our village prays to his idol each morning for bigger interest on his loans, and the poor tenant who owes him just keeps circling like a moth. Doha for this?
doha: moneylender worshipping an idol for more profit, moth is the real devotee
The moth gives its life in love; the moneylender gives a garland and expects a fortune.
washerman, idol, cleansing
The washerman near us bathes the idol of the god every dawn but never washes the thought of cheating customers out of his own mind. A line for him?
doha about a washerman who washes an idol daily but not his own heart
Daily the idol is washed and dressed; the washerman's own heart is never scrubbed

Give me a verse for the washerman who cleans and decorates the carved image of his deity with great devotion, yet leaves the dirt of greed and malice untouched in his own mind, believing the washing is enough.

Please write a doha about the many who bow to carved gods hoping for fortune, though the true paras, the alchemist's touch that transforms iron, is the Name alive in the heart, not a figure on an altar.
My aunt spends her savings on a new idol for the family altar hoping it will bring luck. I told her the paras, the legendary alchemist's touch, is within. Doha for her?
paras, idol
Seeking the paras, the alchemist's touch, they kneel before a carved face; the true alchemy waits in the heart.
doha: idol worship vs the paras, the alchemist's touch, which is the real thing, write it
grindstone, idol, worship
my grandma grinds spices on the grindstone and says it feeds the family more than the idol she bows to. have a doha for that?
The grindstone turns and the family eats; the idol sits silent and no hunger is fed.
doha about the grindstone being more useful than an idol
Say in a doha how the humble grindstone, which turns grain into flour and fills the hungry, deserves more reverence than a carved idol, which only watches the world go by and answers nobody.
Churn the cream of your own heart and butter will rise; no idol has ever churned a hungry belly full.
doha about churn vs idol worship, one gives butter and one gives nothing

Please write a doha about the churn that quietly turns the curd and brings butter, a worthy daily work, and the idol before which people kneel for hours, but which has never produced a single drop for a hungry child.
churn, idol, empty worship
My aunt spends the morning at the idol and the afternoon at her churn, and she says only the churn ever gave her anything. Write something for her.
The lock is on the idol's chamber, and the key is held by the washerman of the rite; while the true Lord is free everywhere.
The washerman who cleans the gods at our local holy place keeps the lock key and charges visitors for a glimpse of the idol. Surely Kabir would have something to say about that.
A doha about a chamber where an idol sits behind a lock, and the washerman who charges a fee for the key, asking how a locked up deity could ever be the Lord of all.
doha: idol behind a lock, washerman holds the key, funny kabir style
idol, lock, washerman
doha about people crossing the water in a boat to worship an idol on the other bank
In the boat they sail to meet a carved face, never guessing the Lord rows within the breast.
We took a boat across to an island to see a famous idol and spent two hours queueing for ten seconds in front of it. Honestly it felt empty. Doha?
A doha on the one who crosses the water by boat to bow before a celebrated idol on the far bank, yet is blind to the Divine presence in the boat that carries him and in every living being.
boat, idol, far worship

A doha about the weaver at his loom weaving cloth to cover a naked idol, applying sandalwood paste to its limbs, never realizing that the one who makes honest cloth with honest hands is nearer to God.
loom, sandalwood, idol
doha: weaver's loom, sandalwood on the idol, who is closer to God
My uncle, a weaver, weaves clothes for the idols in our colony and smears sandalwood on them each festival, yet he says God is nearer when he works the loom. Could you capture that?
Sandalwood anoints the carved image while the weaver's loom hums a truer hymn
Prayer beads in hand, a carved face before him: he turns the round and the idol does not turn toward him.
prayer beads, idol
doha: counting prayer beads in front of an idol and getting nothing back
A doha for the devotee who sits before an idol with prayer beads, counting round after round, hoping the figure will answer or move, while the living God is in his breath and unheard.
Uncle sits for two hours with prayer beads facing the idol and gets mad when anyone interrupts, but the idol never says a word to him. Doha please
Lines about how people clothe, feed and adorn a carved idol with great care, give it new garments each festival, and yet leave the poor child on the road outside hungry and unclothed.
The idol is dressed in silk; a child shivers outside the gates of worship.
At our festival the idol gets a new silk dress and a hundred dishes, and a kid was begging at the entrance in a torn shirt. I cannot forget that. Doha?
doha on dressing idols in silk while real people are cold
silk idol, hungry child
Couplet wanted: the bell that clangs before an idol, the brass noise meant to wake a sleeping god, as if the One who hears the ant's footfall needs to be shaken by a ringing in his ears.
bell, idol, loud worship
The bell is rung to wake the idol; the Lord who is awake in every breath smiles.
My neighbour rings the bell before the idol so hard in the morning that the baby wakes up. Maybe the idol was already awake? Could you write a doha?
doha: ringing a bell to wake an idol makes no sense
tortoise, yogi, idol
Put into verse the yogi who sits still as a tortoise before a carved idol for years, drawing in his senses, but whose inner eye stays closed, because stillness before an image is not seeing God.
There is a yogi at our ghat who sits like a tortoise in front of an idol all day, and kids bring him food, but he never speaks. Can you write a doha on that?
Like the tortoise withdrawn into its shell the yogi sits before the idol, and does not see that the Lord is not in front but within.
doha: yogi sitting like a tortoise in front of an idol for years, still no truth
Our family guru told us to pray to the idol for rain, but as the rainbird calls out loudly for just one drop, I felt the idol never heard anything. Is there a doha for that?
The rainbird cries to the sky, and the answer comes from the sky; the idol before the faithful stays silent.

Please compose a doha in which the rainbird calls from a heart of real longing for the one raindrop and is answered, while the crowd chanting before the idol for rain receives nothing but their own echo.
doha with rainbird and idol, one calls in love the other is just carved
rainbird, idol worship
The cleric says there is no image, the reciter says there is no end to images; both quarrel while the Formless smiles.
doha about the cleric laughing at idols but doing his own show
Something sharp for the cleric who mocks the idol worshippers and calls his own rituals pure, though his pride is a graven image no less, set up in his heart and worshipped every day.
The cleric who lectures our street against idols is just as rigid and proud as the ones he scolds, only he has no statue to hide it. Could you write a doha for him?
cleric, idol, ego

Verse idea: the proud elephant of ego that carries an idol through the streets in a procession while clouds gather above, and everyone cheers the carved image, though no cloud ever rained for the sake of any idol.
The elephant bears the idol on its back, the cloud passes by without a glance.
At our town procession, an elephant carried the idol under dark clouds and people cheered like it was a miracle. Kabir would have laughed. Please write a doha
doha: elephant carrying idol under clouds, everyone cheering, pointless
elephant, cloud, idol parade
doha about how making an idol with hands means the maker is greater than the made, so why bow
made by hands, worshipped
A couplet for how the sculptor chisels an idol with his own tools and then the crowd bows before it, while no one honours the sculptor, and the maker of the maker remains forgotten altogether.
My uncle sculpts idols for a living and says, hesitantly, that he has never felt God in anything he carved. He feels God while eating dinner with us. Doha for him?
The carver made the idol, the worshipper bows; where is the One who made the carver?
bee, idol, honey
Sing of the bee that visits every flower for honey and finds sweetness everywhere, while the devotee sits before one idol with a hungry heart that tastes no sweetness at all.
In our garden, the bees seem happier and more useful than my father in law, who spends the morning at the idol and the evening complaining. A doha?
The bee drinks from a thousand flowers, the pilgrim drinks from none, staring at the idol.
doha: bee gets honey from flowers, we get nothing from idols
idol, voiceless god

Write me a doha about the people who pour their troubles out before the carved idol each morning, who wait for an answer and get silence, and still insist the silence is a blessing and the idol is alive.
You speak and the idol is silent, you weep and the idol does not wipe your tears.
doha about praying to a god that never replies
Sunil prayed for two years to an idol for a job and finally got it by calling a friend. He still gave the idol credit. Can you write a doha on that?
What use to bow to the carved face when the living face of the poor passes you by?
write a kabir doha about idol worship being pointless
A doha on how people spend lakhs on decorating idols with flowers, garlands and grand ceremonies, and meanwhile the hungry neighbour and the old widow on the road go uncared for and unseen.
Our colony collected a big donation for a huge idol for the festival, and the old woman next lane can't afford her medicines. I keep thinking about her. A doha?
idols versus living people
Doha request: the devotee paints a bright forehead mark on an idol each morning and then on his own head, thinking paint brings the divine nearer, though truth is neither on the idol nor the brow.
A forehead mark on the idol's brow, one on his own, and still the sight of God eludes them both.
forehead mark, idol
doha about putting a forehead mark on an idol and calling that worship
My mother spends half an hour putting a forehead mark on every little idol in our altar, but she hasn't looked me in the eye all week. Doha for her?
pearl, snake, idol
A pearl placed upon the idol's brow, a snake coiled around its neck, and the worshipper wonders what is divine.

Couplet please about the ornaments of pearl and the coiled snake draped over an idol, the proud decorations of the faithful, while the pure presence the idol is meant to represent is felt only in a quiet heart.
doha: idol decorated with pearls and a snake garland, lol imagine believing that's god
At the festival, the idol was covered in pearls and a rubber snake. A little girl asked me if God likes ornaments, and I had no answer. Doha for her question?
My father keeps the idol locked in a cabinet with a lock and key so it won't be stolen. Which kind of God needs a lock to be kept safe? A doha please
Locked in a cabinet, guarded by a lock: such a god is a prisoner and he cannot free you.

Verse wanted about the idol that needs a lock to keep thieves away, and the trusting believers who pray to it for protection, never asking how a god who cannot save himself can possibly save anyone else.
doha: lock and key on an idol, god who needs protection lol
idol, lock, guarded god
A beggar came to our holy place and the guard shooed him away from the idol, while we donated money to weigh the idol's ornaments on the scales. What a scene. Doha?
Draw a doha from this: the scales weigh treasure offered to a carved idol while the beggar at the entrance is weighed and found of no worth, though the Lord Himself walks as the beggar.
doha: scales weighing gifts for idol, beggar outside ignored, hypocrisy
On the scales the idol's gifts are weighed; on no scales are the beggar's tears.
scales, beggar, idol worship
idol worship, why bother
doha on why people kneel to a carved figure when God is everywhere
Why bow to a figure carved by hands when the Maker breathes through every breath?
My daughter asked me why we offer food to a statue that never eats it. I was lost for words. Can you give me a doha to answer her?

Tell me in verse of the endless effort of dressing, feeding, bathing, and praying to the statues in the household altar, when the same patient attention given to a living person would bring the true blessing.
carved god, silent god
My grandmother will not eat before she has offered food to the little brass idol, and my grandfather who needs insulin often waits for his meal. A doha?
Couplet on the family that serves the idol first and best at every meal, setting aside the finest dish, while the elder who sits hungry and tired by the hearth is served last.
For the idol, a feast; for the living, the crumbs.
write a doha on feeding idols before real people
At the milk offering ceremony the whole bucket was poured over the idol while kids in the lane begged for a glass. I couldn't stop thinking about the waste. Doha?
Milk flows over the idol and into the drain, and the hungry child is told to wait.
Write a doha on the devotees who pour milk over an idol until it runs into the gutter, believing that it pleases God, while a thin hungry child nearby is turned away without a single sip.
milk, idol, waste
doha: pouring milk on idols while kids go hungry
The washerman sprinkles flowers on the idol each dawn, but a thorn stays in his heart against the neighbour who once insulted him. Kabir doha for this?
doha: washerman washing idol but thorn in his own mind
A doha about the washerman who cleans an idol with water and prayer, making it shine, while a thorn of envy remains in his own heart, a pain worse than any he has washed away.
washerman, thorn, idol
The washerman scrubs the idol's face; the thorn in his own heart still bleeds.

Write a doha on the one-string lute that sings a single note of truth, simple as a thread drawn tight, while the worshippers around the idol clamour with a hundred rituals that only tangle the thread.
one-string lute, thread, idol
doha: one-string lute and thread, simple singing beats worshipping an idol
One thread, one string of a one-string lute, one note: simple music reaches God sooner than a hundred rites before a figure.
The wandering singer at our bus stop plays a one-string lute with a tiny thread tied to it, and says that is his only prayer, no idol needed. Can you do a doha on him?
musk deer, mountain, idol
If worshipping a carved idol brings God, then I would worship a mountain, for a mountain is greater, and the musk deer searches still.
doha: kabir's line about worshipping a mountain instead of an idol, add the musk deer

Retell in a doha how Kabir says that if God can be found by worshipping a carved idol then he would worship the whole mountain, while the musk deer wanders searching for the scent within its own body.
On a trek I saw a musk deer near a huge mountain, and then we came down to a village where everyone bows to a small carved idol. I felt the contrast. Could you capture that in a doha?
A white cloth sheet draped over the idol, a prayer on every lip, yet the shivering poor have no sheet at all.
Every winter my aunt buys a new cloth sheet to cover the idol and the homeless on our road shiver in the cold. I wish there was a doha for her.
doha: cloth sheet covering an idol while people freeze outside
cloth sheet, idol
A couplet that mocks the pious who keep the finest cloth sheet to cover the idol each night against the cold, and think they are very pious, when the true God shivers outside in a thin, torn rag.
doha: if I can find God by worshipping an idol then why not worship the mountain, since it's bigger
If a carved image is God, then the mountain is a greater God; worship that, and be freed.
mountain, idol, worship
Verse that echoes the old saying that if praying to a small carved idol brings God, then one should worship the great mountain itself, so vast and unmoving, and see whether it answers.
We drove past a huge mountain on the way to see a famous idol, and my son asked, 'Why not worship the mountain? It's way bigger.' Doha for his question?
The moneylender donated a huge sum for the new idol, and he is still crushing the tenant farmers, slow as a tortoise but surely. A doha on this?
doha: moneylender and tortoise and idol, hypocrisy of the giver
The tortoise carries its home on its back, the moneylender carries his idol in the marketplace, and neither goes far toward truth.
moneylender, tortoise, idol
Capture in two lines the moneylender who buys a grand idol for the village and bows before it daily, slow and heavy like a tortoise with his shell of greed, while the debts he holds crush the poor.
doha: jaggery on a leaf offered to an idol, then eaten by ants, who is it really for
jaggery, leaf, idol

Compose lines on the jaggery and the leaf offered with ritual before an idol, which the ants and the reciter's family enjoy afterwards, while the idol remains untouched, the offering a pleasing story for the offerer.
We offered jaggery on a leaf at the idol and my son asked who actually eats it. I said the reciter's family. He said, 'Then why not give it to them directly?' Doha for his logic?
Jaggery on a green leaf before an idol, sweetness wasted on a mouth that does not eat.

Write a doha on the many who believe that only bowing before a certain stern-faced figure in a particular place will earn mercy, never understanding that the Lord who made all places is found in none more than another.
idols can't answer
Before the carved face they bow in hope, and the face looks on with the same blank smile.
My neighbour travels three hours to bow to a particular idol, and doesn't visit his dying mother who lives two lanes away. Doha for him?
write a doha on worshipping carved figures
The idol is carved and the carver sleeps; the worshipper bows and the world turns on.
why worship idols
doha on carved gods vs the real God inside you
An old village woman told me, 'I have been talking to the idol for sixty years and it has never answered; I think I should have talked to my husband.' Doha for her?
Write a doha about the long years people give to idol worship, bowing, offering, praying, and begging, and at the end of life finding that all they gave to the carved image was never returned by it.
A rope was used to tie the idol onto the cart for the procession, and jaggery was passed out afterwards, and a man next to me wondered aloud who was carrying whom. A doha?

Write a doha on the rope that ties the idol to its cart and the jaggery distributed at the festival, the ceremonies that bind people more tightly than any rope, to a God who is never found in the knots.
rope, jaggery, idol
doha: rope on an idol cart, jaggery sweets afterwards, the real God is not in the parade
A rope binds the idol to the cart, and jaggery binds the people to the idol, but what binds the Soul to God?
idol, deaf and dumb god
What blessing can the carved face give, when it has never opened its eyes to see its own devotees?
Write a doha about the devotee who asks an idol to see his troubles, hear his prayers and bless his work, though the idol has no ears to hear, no eyes to see, and no lips to answer.
My brother gave his savings to a big idol ceremony and now cannot pay his rent. The idol did not say a word. Is there a doha for his regret?
doha about worshipping idols that can't see or hear
yo write a doha about the folly of worshipping a carved figure
idol, foolish worship
He carved the god and then he bowed to it, and called the carver wise.
Write a doha about a man who spends weeks carving an idol with great skill, sets it on the altar, and then falls down at its feet to pray for guidance he could have found by looking inside himself.
My friend is an art student who sculpted a goddess for a class project, and then her grandmother started worshipping it daily. Everyone laughs, but I feel it says something. Doha?
bitter gourd, idol, sweetness
doha: bitter gourd offered to an idol, still bitter, like worship without change
Wash the bitter gourd a hundred times and it stays bitter; bow to a hundred idols and the heart stays unchanged.
My mother made a special bitter gourd dish as an offering to the idol and then complained it was too bitter. I joked that the idol must have thought so too. A doha?
Write a doha on how the bitter gourd stays bitter no matter how many times it is washed, and a heart that has not changed stays bitter however many idols its owner worships with ritual.
My niece asked me, 'Why do we worship a statue if God is invisible?' I had no good answer. Could you give me a doha to say to her?
idol, what for
The Invisible lives in every breath, yet we bow to a figure with eyes of paint.
Write a doha about the question of why we kneel before a figure made by hands when the Lord is said to be formless, present in all, beyond name, and not confined within any carving.
doha about a formless God and people worshipping statues anyway
Gods of metal and carved wood stand in a row, mute guests at a feast that is eaten by others.
idol worship doha please, kabir style
idols, silence
Write a doha on how rows of carved gods line the walls of the family room, each given flowers and incense daily, yet none ever moves, speaks, or lifts the weight of sorrow from a single worshipper.
At my wedding, my in laws insisted on a ceremony with ten different idols. It took five hours and I felt nothing. Can you give me a doha about that?
thread, leaf, idol

Write a doha about the sacred thread tied around the idol and the green leaf placed upon it, simple objects dressed up as holy, offered daily with pomp yet carrying no more truth than a leaf on the ground.
A thread around the idol's neck, a leaf before its feet: small offerings to a figure that does not notice.
My granny ties a thread around the idol every morning and puts a fresh leaf in front of it, as if the idol would mind if she forgot. Can you write a doha on this?
doha: thread and leaf offered to an idol, just stuff, not God
Compose a doha about the churn in the kitchen turned with honest effort to bring forth butter, and the idol in the corner that has no effort and no gift; yet we reserve our devotion for the latter.
churn, idol, honest work
doha: churn works, idol doesn't, kabir would say
The churn turns and the butter rises; the idol sits and only the dust gathers.
My grandma was proud of her butter churn and said it gave more blessings than any idol. Everyone laughed but she was serious. Could you make a doha from that?
The yogi chants to a carved face and the moneylender counts coins in front of one; both bow to the same silence.

Write a doha on the yogi and the moneylender who both bow before the same carved idol, one asking for liberation and the other for gain, and the idol answers neither because it is only wood and paint.
doha: yogi and moneylender both worship an idol, want different things
At the idol ceremony yesterday I saw a yogi praying for liberation next to a moneylender praying for profit, and both looked equally sincere. Doha?
yogi, moneylender, idol

Compose a doha on the churn that brings butter and the winnowing fan that separates grain from husk, honest tools of the household, which do more good than the idol before which people spend whole days in prayer.
churn, winnowing fan, idol
The winnowing fan lifts the husk away, the churn lifts the butter; what has the idol ever lifted?
doha: churn and winnowing fan are more useful than an idol
My grandmother used the churn and the winnowing fan every day and said these were her prayers, while my uncle spent hours worshipping the idol. Could you write something on this?
traveler, tree, idol
doha: traveler rests under a tree, finds more peace than before an idol
Write a doha on the weary traveler who rests under the shade of a tree and feels the peace of the Lord, while his rich neighbour pays to be let in for a glimpse of an idol and feels nothing.
The traveler found God in the shade of a tree, while the crowd waited for hours to see a carved face.
On our trip, a traveler shared his food under a tree with us, and I felt more blessing than at the famous idol we visited the day before. Could you write a doha on that?
The yogi in our village worships a different idol each day of the week and says that makes him more holy, but he cannot sit with a single thought in peace. A doha?
yogi, many idols
A god for each day, a prayer for each god, and the yogi's mind a restless crowd of desires.
doha: yogi switching idols every day, still restless

Write a doha about the yogi who changes his idol every day of the week, believing each one brings a different gift, never realising that the restless mind which seeks all of them is the very thing to be calmed.
skeleton, idol, life
When the skeleton lies bare and the carved idol still stands, what is the difference between them but breath?
At my uncle's last rites, I looked at his skeleton-thin hands and realized the idol he prayed to for fifty years was still standing exactly as before, unmoved. Could you write a doha for this?
doha: skeleton and idol, both silent, one was alive though
Write a doha on the skeleton that was once a living devotee and the idol it worshipped, both silent now, one made by hands and one by God, and only one ever truly knew love.
